overall: Committee violated the OML because all but one member lacked required certification forms; the minutes-request allegation was found to be a Public Records Law request, and website posting was declined.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to respond to a request for meeting minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that this request was made under the Public Records Law, and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged committee members had not completed their Open Meeting Law certification forms.
allegations.key_passage: Because all but one Committee member failed to complete the required Open Meeting Law certifications, we find the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to post meeting minutes to the town website; the AG declined to review because website posting is not required.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website, but rather that meeting minutes be made available within 10 days of a request.

allegations.summary: Not raised by complaint; AG noted committee approved minutes of three 2020 meetings untimely and issued a reminder.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee did not approve minutes of its April 23, 2020, May 8, 2020, and May 15, 2020, meetings in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
All committee members except the one who had a valid certification must review the Open Meeting Law, AG regulations, the OML Guide, and relevant determinations from the last five years.
Those members must certify their review on the AG form, file it with the Town Clerk within 14 days, and email a copy to the AG's office within 14 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
